The Lloyds Bank coprolite is a large coprolite, or fossilised specimen of human faeces, recovered by the York Archaeological Trust while excavating the settlement of Jórvík in northern England. 
The specimen was dated around the 9th century and offers insight into the dietary practices of the Anglo-Scandinavians during this period.

A natural nuclear fission reactor is a uranium deposit where self-sustaining nuclear chain reactions occur through natural geological processes rather than human construction. The possibility of such reactors existing in situ within an ore body moderated by groundwater was proposed by Paul Kuroda in 1956.
